evaluations.label: A
errors: Spells the organizer's name 'Andrei' and the building 'UniMile' (transcript: Andre, Unimail)
'Susan and Martin both raised concerns about sharing offices' - Martin said he had nothing against sharing; only Susan voiced a concern
Next meeting framed as 'discussed' rather than agreed (Tuesday ~2 p.m. was agreed)
strengths: Correct core facts: 15 people / ~18 positions, 16 slots if a 2P room becomes the reading room, zero growth, fixed room count but open assignment
Correct owners for the two clearest actions (Andre checks room separation; Susan asks Maggie and Pierrette)
Clearly separates what was decided from what remains open (lounge purpose, Gisela placement)
Timestamps and attributions generally match the transcript
weaknesses: Omits Andre's follow-ups on fitting 4 places in a 3P room and asking whether Gisela can sit with the school's other admin
Does not mention the idea of placing Gisela with the school admin down the hall
Everyone's homework (bring a sketch/proposal) is in the body but not in the action items list

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'merge proposals with another group before next Tuesday's review meeting' - merging with the other group comes after the next meeting
Action item assigns following up with Maggie and Pierrette to Andrei; Susan volunteered for this
'Distribute documents... to all participants' listed as an action item; Andre handed them out during the meeting
'Management recognizes this [lounge] as a priority due to previously lengthy discussions' - unsupported; the lounge's role was explicitly left open and Susan questioned the need
'desk arrangements inside rooms can be flexible' - what is flexible is assignment of people to rooms
'Smoking is allowed only outside, even on balconies' - garbled; balcony is where smoking is allowed
'no dedicated cafeteria' contradicts its own line that the building's cafeteria closes at 5
'expects to manage this through proposals... rather than direct surveys' - Martin also proposed asking each person for their own place
Several timestamps misplaced (e.g., building-modification points cited at 19:34)
strengths: Very broad coverage: furniture, part-time, reading room debate, Gisela options incl. school admin idea, 4-in-3P idea, coffee/cafeteria, smoking, next meeting Tuesday ~14:00
Includes Andre's investigation items on room splitting, 4 desks and admin placement
weaknesses: Highly repetitive and padded (growth/visitor and building-permission points restated across sections)
Wrong owner on the Maggie/Pierrette follow-up and a non-action listed as an action
Overstates the lounge as a settled priority
Hard to scan for a reader who missed the meeting

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Strong support for a dedicated lounge/reading room' - Susan questioned whether it was needed; support was not uniform
'Majority lean toward a mixed-use room' - only Martin (and some unnamed people) and Susan's overflow point; no majority was established
strengths: Concise and accurate on the key numbers (15 people, ~18 positions, 16 slots with a 2P reading room, zero growth)
Captures all of Andre's follow-ups: room separation, 4 desks in a 3P room, Gisela with another school admin
Correctly notes the professor-assistant sharing tradition cannot be imposed, Susan's confidential rectorate work, Martin's phone calls
Next meeting details correct, including the MDM meeting in the morning at Unimail and ~2 PM
weaknesses: Next steps have no owners (Andre's checks and Susan's outreach to Maggie and Pierrette are unattributed)
Mild overstatement of consensus on the lounge

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'accommodate approximately 15 to 18 people' - there are 15 people and ~18 positions
'noting this is common in other faculties but not necessarily here' - reversed: sharing with assistants is a tradition at this school; other faculties give professors their own offices
Uses 'Speaker 1/3/4' labels that do not match the transcript's A/B/C/D, making attributions unverifiable and confusing
'Action Items (none)' - Andre committed to checking room separation, Susan to asking Maggie and Pierrette, everyone to bring proposals
'Members were tasked with consulting colleagues, such as Maggie and Pierrette' - Susan specifically volunteered
Lounge described as a 'significant requirement... to serve as a meeting or overflow space' - its purpose was left open
'negotiation with other groups in the building' - only one other group was mentioned
strengths: Correctly lists the open questions (partitioning, 4 in a 3P room, lounge function)
Captures furniture and equipment constraints and next meeting Tuesday 2 PM
weaknesses: Empty action items section contradicts its own outline
Reversed fact on professor office norms
Redundant summary and outline repeat the same content

rationale: C and A are both accurate and readable; C edges ahead by capturing all of Andre's follow-ups (room separation, 4 desks in a 3P room, Gisela with school admin) and the full next-meeting logistics, though it omits owners. A has correct owners but misses two of Andre's checks and mislabels Martin as raising concerns about sharing. B is the most exhaustive but repetitive, assigns the Maggie/Pierrette follow-up to the wrong person, lists a non-action, and misstates the sequence of merging with the other group. D has an empty action items list, reversed the professor office norm, conflates 15 people with 18 slots, and uses speaker numbers that do not map to the transcript.
